one_liner: FP32 GEMM emulated with bf16 matrix-core products on AMD MI250; 1.20-1.22x over per-shape-tuned rocBLAS sgemm at a lower accuracy tier.
what_it_does: A small C/HIP library (src/emugemm.h, src/emugemm.cpp) that computes row-major C = A*B for FP32 inputs on AMD CDNA by splitting A and B into BF16 or FP16 hi/lo slices, running three low-precision rocBLAS GEMMs on the matrix cores, and accumulating them in FP32. You pass a requested max_rel_err; a planner picks native FP32, FP32 with K-chunks summed in FP64, bf16x3 or fp16x3, and returns a plan whose reason string says 'TARGET UNREACHABLE' when no scheme meets the request. It is not a drop-in rocblas_sgemm: own entry point emugemm_sgemm(handle, M, N, K, A, B, C, &req, &hints, &plan), row-major, no transposes, alpha=1, beta=0 only, and it needs a per-GPU, per-ROCm tuning table loaded by emugemm_init.
how_it_is_fast: Multiword (split-precision) GEMM emulation in the line of Markidis 2018, Ootomo and Yokota 2022, and Fasi-Higham et al. 2023: each FP32 value x becomes s0 = bf16(x) and s1 = bf16(x - s0), and C = A0*B0 + A0*B1 + A1*B0 (the small A1*B1 term is dropped). On MI250 the bf16 MFMA rate is 3.98x the FP32 MFMA rate (169.2 vs 42.5 TFLOP/s measured), so three bf16 products cost about 0.75 of one FP32 product, a ceiling of 1.33x; the repo reaches 1.20-1.22x of it. Solution tuning is what makes the bf16 side reach that rate: an offline table (data/tune_table.csv, 820 rows) maps shapes to rocBLAS solution indices via rocblas_gemm_algo_solution_index, because the default rocBLAS bf16 kernel choice ran as low as 83.9 TFLOP/s versus 137.8 for the best solution at the MLP shape.
when_to_use: Large FP32 GEMMs (thousands per side, e.g. 8192x28672x8192 or 12288^3) on an MI250 / gfx90a GCD where about 4.5e-6 normwise relative error is acceptable.
GEMM-bound pipelines; the repo's CholeskyQR2 randomized SVD got 1.19x end to end at a 1e-5 target, while a Householder-QR pipeline gained only 1.8% because GEMM was 300 of 6192 ms.
Inputs with wide dynamic range where you want FP32's 8-bit exponent kept (bf16 path) rather than fp16 scaling tricks.
All-positive or non-cancelling data (counts, histograms, convolutions): Round 9 measured bf16x3 4x more accurate than FP32 at K=65536 on U(0,1) inputs.

As a template for tuning rocBLAS itself: the tuning-table and solution-index plumbing (and the ROCm/rocm-libraries#9985 evidence) show where the default rocBLAS heuristic leaves 1.3-4.5x on skinny or large-K shapes.
when_not_to_use: When you need bit-for-bit or better-than-native FP32 accuracy: bf16x3 has a hard floor of 4.4355e-6, worse than native FP32 at K=8192 (4.49e-6 vs 1.62e-6 in the repo's own table); below the floor the planner falls back to FP32 with FP64 chunk sums, which is slower than native.

Strongly cancelling products (large rho = || |A||B| || / ||AB||): bf16x3 error grew to 1.65e-3 (35x FP32) in Round 9 and peaked at 31.5x FP32 near rho = 1.2e4 in Round 10; the planner probes rho with 64 Rademacher vectors (about 1.6% extra cost) and may then refuse or escalate.

Any GPU other than gfx90a: every model constant and the tuning table were measured on MI250 with ROCm 7.2.3; the README says CDNA3/CDNA4 may invert the conclusions, and on CDNA2 FP64 emulation is a loss.

Small shapes: scan and split passes (one read of A and B plus two low-precision copies) cost more than the GEMM saves; the planner then returns native FP32 (the doc cites 2048x2048x4096 at 1.39 ms vs 1.03 ms before that fix).
Production code needing transposes, alpha/beta, batched calls, column-major layout or concurrency from several host threads: none of these is supported.

integration.dependencies: ROCm (tested 7.2.3) with HIP and rocBLAS; rocSOLVER only for the randsvd2 example; a tuning table generated by bench/gen_tune_table.cpp for your GPU and ROCm version
integration.min_toolchain: hipcc from ROCm 7.2.3 (only version tested); C++ (std::vector, lambdas, so C++11 or later); C-compatible extern "C" API
integration.platforms: AMD CDNA GPUs; only gfx90a (MI250) tested
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the code keeps the workspace buffers and tuning table in unsynchronized file-scope globals, so concurrent calls from several host threads are unsafe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different entry point and signature from rocblas_sgemm; row-major, non-transposed, alpha=1, beta=0 only; results are not bit-identical to FP32

gotchas: Unless you pass a_absmax, b_absmax and rho in emu_hints_t, every call runs an absmax scan and a 64-probe rho estimate, each ending in a blocking hipMemcpy; reuse the hints struct (the call writes measured values back) to pay this once. The a_is_reused flag is declared but the code does not cache splits.
Split, scan and accumulate kernels launch on the default (null) stream, not on the rocBLAS handle's stream, and kernel launch errors are not checked.

emugemm_init reads the architecture of device 0, not the current device, and with no table file it runs untuned (the code warns up to 1.7x slower bf16); shapes farther than a log2 distance of 1 from any table row fall back to the rocBLAS default solution.

The headline 1.20-1.22x came from emu_tuned.cpp, which is not in the repository; the published bench/emugemm_test.cpp times three back-to-back calls with no warm-up against an untuned rocblas_gemm_ex default, so it does not reproduce the headline table.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only catalogued GEMM entry for AMD Instinct GPUs: pick it over the NVIDIA-only blackwell-tensorcore-kernels, gpu-compute and CUDA-L2 when you are on an MI250, have FP32 data, and can accept about 4.5e-6 error in exchange for about 1.2x.
verified_claims_summary: On one MI250 GCD with ROCm 7.2.3 and hipcc -O3 --offload-arch=gfx90a, the author's emu_tuned harness measured bf16x3 at 45.33, 44.26 and 45.06 TFLOP/s against per-shape-tuned rocBLAS FP32 at 37.52, 37.03 and 37.02 (1.21x, 1.20x, 1.22x) on 8192x28672x8192, 16384x8192x8192 and 12288^3, and 325.1 vs 278.4 TFLOP/s (1.17x) with all 8 GCDs at 8192^3. These are first-party numbers from an unpublished harness, measured before the 2026-08-13 timing-error fixes, and they compare against FP32 that is about 2.8x more accurate at those K.
status_note: Active single-author research repo (MIT, 0 stars, last commit 2026-09-03, no issues filed), unusually candid about its own corrected numbers; small enough to vendor, but treat it as a measured prototype for gfx90a rather than a maintained library.
